I added `GET /api/admin/users/recently-created`, which returns the logins of users created in the last 7 days. I didn't run the build or any tests, as you asked.

- **Repository:** `UserRepository` has a new derived query, `findAllByCreatedDateAfter(Instant)`. The caller passes the cutoff, as `docs/persistence.md` requires.
- **Service:** `UserService.getRecentlyCreatedUserLogins()` works out the cutoff as now minus 7 days, using an injected `Clock`. It runs in a read-only transaction and returns the logins as `List<String>`.
- **Clock:** `src/main/java/CLAUDE.md` requires `Clock` injection, and the project had no `Clock` bean. I added `config/ClockConfiguration` with `Clock.systemUTC()` and added a `Clock` constructor argument to `UserService`. Nothing in `src` calls `new UserService(...)`, so no manual construction needed updating.
- **Resource:** `UserResource.getRecentlyCreatedUsers()` is mapped to `/users/recently-created` and has the same `@PreAuthorize` admin check as the other admin methods. The literal path is declared before `/users/{login}`, so it takes precedence.

`docs/backend.md` says REST endpoints should never return unbounded lists. This one is bounded only by the 7-day window, so a burst of sign-ups could make it large. I kept the plain list you asked for. If you want it paged, I can switch it to `Pageable` with pagination headers.

I didn't add tests.
